title: What’s different in {language}
summary: The few things in {language} that will feel different from {best}, and what will feel familiar.

differences.title: What’s different
differences.body: Here’s what will feel new. One at a time.

complete.title: Now you know what to expect
complete.body: Gef thinks that went rather well.

labels.trait.noun_gender.title: Gender
labels.trait.noun_gender.two: In {language}, every noun is masculine or feminine, and the words around it have to match.
labels.trait.noun_gender.three: In {language}, every noun is masculine, feminine or neuter, and the words around it have to match.
labels.trait.articles.title: Little words like “the” and “a”
labels.trait.articles.definite_only: {language} has a word for “the” but none for “a”.
labels.trait.formal_you.title: Formal and informal “you”
labels.trait.formal_you.none: {language} has no separate polite “you”: you speak to everyone the same way.
labels.trait.formal_you.distinct: {language} has a polite “you” and a friendly “you”, and you choose between them.
labels.trait.verb_endings.title: Verb endings
labels.trait.verb_endings.few: In {language}, verbs barely change with the subject.
labels.trait.verb_endings.many: In {language}, verbs take many different endings: for tense, politeness or who is acting.
labels.trait.subject_pronouns.title: Dropping “I” and “you”
labels.trait.subject_pronouns.often_dropped: {language} often leaves out “I” and “you”, because the verb ending already says who.
labels.trait.adjective_position.title: Where describing words go
labels.trait.adjective_position.before_noun: In {language}, adjectives usually come before the noun.
labels.trait.adjective_position.after_noun: In {language}, adjectives usually come after the noun.
labels.trait.adjective_position.either: In {language}, adjectives can come before or after the noun.
labels.trait.cases.title: Endings on nouns
labels.trait.cases.none: {language} nouns don’t change for their role in the sentence.
labels.trait.cases.pronouns_only: In {language}, only pronouns change for their role in the sentence.
labels.trait.cases.some: In {language}, nouns, articles and adjectives change form for their role in the sentence ({count} cases).
labels.trait.word_order.title: Word order
labels.trait.word_order.svo: {language} normally puts the subject first, then the verb, then the object.
labels.trait.word_order.flexible: In {language}, word order is flexible, because endings show who does what.
labels.trait.questions.title: Asking questions
labels.trait.questions.auxiliary_do: {language} adds a helper word like “do” to make a question.
labels.trait.questions.intonation_or_inversion: {language} can make a question just by raising your voice or swapping the word order, with no “do” needed.
labels.q.which_formal: Which sentence is the formal one?
labels.trait.word_building.title: How words are built
labels.trait.word_building.isolating: {language} words hardly change: small separate words and word order do the work that endings do elsewhere.
labels.trait.word_building.inflecting: In {language}, words change their endings to show things like who, when and how many.
labels.trait.word_building.agglutinating: {language} builds words by stacking small pieces onto a root, so one long word can be a whole sentence.
labels.trait.word_building.root_and_pattern: {language} builds many words from a root of consonants slotted into patterns of vowels, so related words look and sound alike.
labels.trait.noun_gender.classes: In {language}, nouns belong to classes ({count}) shown by a prefix, and the words around a noun match its class.
labels.trait.classifiers.title: Counting words
labels.trait.classifiers.none: {language} counts things the way you do, with no extra word.
labels.trait.classifiers.required: In {language}, you can’t put a number straight in front of a noun: you add a counting word between them.
labels.trait.formal_you.levels: {language} has several levels of politeness built into its verbs and words.
labels.trait.verb_endings.none: In {language}, verbs never change their form.
labels.trait.dual_number.title: Two of something
labels.trait.dual_number.present: {language} has a special form for exactly two of something, besides singular and plural.
labels.trait.questions.particle: {language} can turn a statement into a question with a small question word.
labels.trait.subject_pronouns.context_dependent: {language} often leaves out “I” and “you” when the context makes it clear who is meant.
labels.trait.word_order.sov: {language} normally puts the verb at the end: the subject, then the object, then the verb.
labels.trait.word_order.vso: {language} often puts the verb first, before the subject.
